answer: Two agents claim two towns. At an hour neither can predict, the network asks what the sky is doing overhead. An echo rolls over the oasis at dusk, and the agent under a jade sky sees another. Each answer is checked against the nearest weather station, and a mismatch ends the identity at once. A farm under one roof reports one sky a thousand times, so faking it needs a thousand roofs, about $400 a month each. Cheap stations drift, so one real reading in forty fails and is retried.
